As the oligocene and eocene formations have been drilled in 26 hole, the so-called Gumbo formation is already covered by 20 casing. Nevertheless, the day-stones to be drilled are reputed as being difficult due to problems arising during penetration. They hydrate easily and eventually come apart and, if the mud is not

rfectly suited to this type of formation, may lead to redrilling and caving. The mud used in this stage must therefore respond to the following essential criteria: - Have such specific gravity as to contain the slight tendency to creep in of the shales.
